messages:
anna: Quick sync — we need to settle capacity handoff rules for dedicated -> hosted overflow when a region pool saturates. Proposal below, want opinions before I put an RFC in.

ravi: +1 for a clear policy. can you outline the decision order you're thinking? region preference, tier checks, data isolation? :thinking_face:

anna: Yep. Draft decision order: 1) if dedicated capacity in same region has spare low-latency slots, use that; 2) otherwise try hosted pool in same region and same customer tier (e.g., enterprise), 3) next try hosted same-region best-effort, 4) cross-region hosted only if caller allows cross-region flag. Also add an opt-out for "no-hosted-fallback" for customers with strict data boundaries.

leo: Two immediate red flags: (a) how do we represent "same customer tier" across hosted pools? billing tier != SLA tier. (b) telemetry - how do we attribute calls/costs back to tenant when routed to hosted?

sara: For (a) we can tag hosted pool nodes with capacity_labels: {tier: enterprise, compliance: pci}. The router can filter pools by labels. For (b) we must propagate tenant headers and emit tenant-scoped metrics. we already carry X-RW-Tenant in requests.

jun: Important: KMS/HSM constraints. If a tenant uses customer-managed keys on their Dedicated, we cannot route plaintext payloads to hosted. So the router needs to short-circuit if request contains header X-RW-KMS: cmk. That should mean immediate rejection or queueing to dedicated-only.

anna: Agreed. Add a rule: if X-RW-KMS present -> no-hosted-fallback. Same for data-class=pii. Also propose an API param for customers + console toggle: overflow_policy: ["never","region-only","best-effort"]. default for Dedicated is "region-only".

ravi: UX: console should show a per-tenant "handoff budget" and an audit timeline when handoffs occur. product wants a toggle to allow customers to opt into best-effort overflow with clear SLA degradation messaging.

leo: On metrics: propose counters and histograms: rw.handoff.attempts, rw.handoff.success, rw.handoff.downgrade_latency_ms, rw.handoff.tag={region,reason,policy}. Also emit rw.route.variant with model_variant id so we can see when a different variant was used during handoff.

sara: We should annotate traces with trace attributes: routing.choice and routing.reason. Add event when we downgrade model_variant (e.g., quantized-8bit instead of high-precision) with the exact fallback chain. That will help QA/alerts.

jun: Security: please make sure hosted fallback does not traverse customer VPC subnets or cross private networks. Hosted nodes must only access public inference endpoints and respect egress rules. If we ever do cross-region for private deployments, that's a hard no unless customer explicitly enabled it.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new router config schema proposed: { "overflow_policy": "region-only|best-effort|never", "allow_cross_region": true|false, "model_variant_fallback": ["exact","compatible-variant","small-quant"], "label_filters": ["tier","compliance"] }

anna: I also want safe defaults: Dedicated tenants default to "region-only" and "compatible-variant" fallback chain, with a max allowed deviation of 25% estimated latency increase. If exceeded, we should prefer queueing to busy dedicated pool and send notification rather than auto-fallback.

ravi: How do we compute "estimated latency increase"? We need a simulator or a heuristic based on p50/p95 of candidate pools + additional network hop. Might be hard to get accurate across regions.

leo: We can use historical profiling: each pool reports p50/p95 per model_variant. Router uses weighted sum: route_latency = pool_p50 + network_overhead(region_distance). Keep it conservative.

sara: Rollouts UX: in the console's rollout page, add a 'handoff preview' that shows percent of requests that would overflow under current traffic and capacity. Also allow A/B toggling overflow_policy for a tenant for X days to collect data.

jun: Edge case: what about tenants with pinned model_versions? If they pin a version not present in hosted pools, variant fallback must be blocked unless they opt-in. We must surface that in the API error: 409 + message: "pinned model not available in fallback pools".

anna: Good call. We'll add a hard-policy: pin = strict unless tenant sets pin_policy="allow-variant-fallback". Console will surface pin_policy prominently.

ravi: Quotas: if we allow overflow, hosted pool's quotas must account for delegated dedicated traffic. We need a per-tenant token bucket that sums across dedicated+hosted usage and enforces global quota.

leo: Implementation note: router will annotate request with X-RW-Routing-Path: dedicated->hosted.eu-west->variant:fast-quant and also attach X-RW-Routed-From: <pool-id>. This helps billing and audit.

sara: Alerting: create an alert when handoff rate > 5% for any enterprise tenant in a week or when median model_variant downgrade count exceeds threshold.

anna: Next steps: I'll file RFC with these rules. Action items: leo to prototype router scoring function, sara to draft telemetry key names and trace attributes, jun to enumerate KMS+data flags that block fallback, ravi to mock console toggles and handoff budget UI.

leo: I'll start a spike today — will post logs and a small simulation later this afternoon. :rocket:

sara: I'll add telemetry stubs to the router branch and a sample dashboard showing handoff heatmap.

jun: I'll validate KMS flow and produce a short doc of headers that must be honored.

anna: Thanks everyone. Let's sync in the RFC review tomorrow at 11. If anyone thinks "never allow hosted fallback for all dedicated customers" is preferable, reply here now because product will need to know.

ravi: I'm OK with defaults as long as opt-out is easy and clearly labeled. :+1:

ops-bot: meeting-scheduler: RFC review scheduled for 1712436400 (tomorrow 11:00).
